    kavach-rs sqlx_migrate gating tests — ambient-env isolation fix (DIAGNOSED + PATCH READY, blocked on installed-gate cross-repo mismatch) 2026-06-11.

CONTEXT: while making the §CENTRALIZED_CONFIG env::var gate live (decision.arch.centralized-config-gate-shipped), `cargo nextest -p kavach-engine` showed 3 PRE-EXISTING failures (not caused by the env::var arm).

[RCA]
symptom: 3 tests FAIL on dev — sqlx_migrate::tests::gating::{blocks_sqlx_migrate_run_without_rca, matches_cargo_sqlx_variant, real_run_still_blocks_after_introspection_whitelist} ("must block" asserts get None).
repro: cargo nextest -p kavach-engine sqlx_migrate; PASS with `env -u DATABASE_URL -u KAVACH_LOCAL_DB` prefix.
why1: check_sqlx_migrate_requires_rca short-circuits to None when KAVACH_LOCAL_DB=1 (line 77) | the dev shell sources .env which sets KAVACH_LOCAL_DB=1.
why2: the 3 "must block" tests read KAVACH_LOCAL_DB/DATABASE_URL from the AMBIENT process env, never neutralizing it | only local_db_override_bypasses uses temp_env.
why3: test fixtures depend on the runner's environment | §TESTING violation (no ambient-env dependence).
root_cause: test-isolation defect — gate LOGIC is correct, the tests fail to clear the env the gate reads. PASS on clean CI, FAIL on dev with KAVACH_LOCAL_DB set.
blast_radius: 3 tests in crates/kavach-engine/src/gates/pre_tool_bash/write_bypass/sqlx_migrate/tests/gating.rs.
fix: wrap each "must block" assertion in a hermetic helper.

READY PATCH (gating.rs) — add helper + wrap the 3 tests:
```
fn with_production_env(f: impl FnOnce()) {
    temp_env::with_vars(
        [("KAVACH_LOCAL_DB", None::<&str>), ("DATABASE_URL", None::<&str>)],
        f,
    );
}
```
Then wrap each of blocks_sqlx_migrate_run_without_rca / matches_cargo_sqlx_variant / real_run_still_blocks_after_introspection_whitelist bodies in `with_production_env(|| { <existing asserts> });`. (temp_env 0.3 with_vars: None removes the var for the closure; proven in-repo at local_db.rs. research.temp-env-with-vars-hermetic-test.)

VERIFIED (proof the fix is correct): `env -u DATABASE_URL -u KAVACH_LOCAL_DB cargo nextest -p kavach-engine sqlx_migrate::tests::gating` → 12/12 PASS. The hermetic wrapper makes that neutralization intrinsic to the 3 tests.

[decision] decision.arch.harness-rlaif-strict-deferral-penalty — Strict RLAIF: deferral/false-blocker handoff scores -12 (cannot be judged good) (status: done, access: 0)
    Spec parent: roadmap.unit.infra.kavach-harness-self-improvement
GOAL: the RLAIF reward scorer must penalize the deferral/false-blocker handoff class so a turn that routes doable work back to the user can NEVER be judged "good".

SHIPPED (this iteration, 3-witness): kavach-patterns/src/reward.rs
- DEFERRAL_HANDOFF_PENALTY = -12 (below any single real-build +10).
- DEFERRAL_RE: case-insensitive regex over EventKind::Stop.final_message matching the global CLAUDE.md forbidden_handoff_phrases ("the next step is yours", "start a new session", "in another session", "you should run", "over to you", "cannot ... from this session", "the work must run in").
- score_event Stop arm: DEFERRAL_RE match -> DEFERRAL_HANDOFF_PENALTY, else 0.
- 4 new tests (reward_test.rs): clean_stop=0, deferral=-12, cannot-from-session=-12, handoff_turn_cannot_outscore_a_real_build. 19/19 pass; cargo check + clippy clean.

ROOT CAUSE: prior scorer scored Stop events 0 unconditionally - the most damaging failure (handing back ordered work) was UNSCORED, so a false-blocker turn netted >=0 and RLAIF judged it "+1.0 good". RCA mistake.false-fence-handoff-2026-06-17.

RESIDUAL (filed as children, not silent):
- semantic deferral detector (LLM-judge) - regex misses paraphrased handoffs.
- balance-sheet LEDGER: persist each scored turn as a kavach record (debit=mistakes/penalties, credit=verified work) for durable learning-awareness.
- gate de-gating: remove residual stale_blocker/has_inert_blocker owner-gate machinery so dispatch = status+deps+umbrella only.

[decision] decision.arch.kavach-depends-on-rpc-mirror-code-shipped-runtime-pending — Daemon-side --depends-on content mirror: code shipped+tested at correct layer; runtime not yet observed; content-line is the live mechanism (status: todo, access: 0)
    CORRECTION (2026-06-17, verified by live test): the --depends-on content-mirror
fix shipped to kavach-cli (cmd/db/write.rs::mirror_depends_on_into_content) does
NOT take effect for `kavach db write`, because that command routes through the
DAEMON RPC write handler (kavach-rpc), not the CLI's cmd/db/write.rs::run. The
CLI-side mirror runs only on the rare direct-DB fallback path (daemon down). On
the normal RPC path the daemon writes the row, and the daemon has no mirror — so
a --depends-on-only gate still stores empty/flagless content and the card stays
RUNNABLE. PROVEN: re-ran `kavach db write … --depends-on X` (binary reinstalled +
verified to contain the fn); content had no DEPENDS_ON line; card stayed READY.

CORRECT FIX LAYER (follow-up): move the mirror into the RPC write method
(kavach-rpc methods/roadmap write handler) OR into the shared
upsert_entry_full/write path both the CLI-direct and RPC paths call — so the
DEPENDS_ON content line is injected server-side regardless of entry path. The CLI
helper + its 6 passing tests stay valid for the direct path; they just don't cover
the dominant RPC path.

WORKING CONTRACT TODAY (daemon-honored): gate a card with a literal `DEPENDS_ON:
<key>` LINE in --content (the daemon write handler persists content verbatim;
dispatch readiness parses it). This is what every gated card this session used
successfully (BDF, async-stripe, grpc-retire, live-prayer, MESH E4 — all verified
WAITING). The --depends-on FLAG remains for graph edges + the direct path.

Supersedes the "shipped+live" claim in
decision.arch.kavach-depends-on-content-mirror-shipped: the code shipped + tests
pass + binary deployed, but it does not cover the RPC write path that
`kavach db write` actually uses. Net effect on the loop: unchanged until the RPC-
layer fix lands; the content-line workaround is the live mechanism.

[decision] mistake.false-fence-handoff-2026-06-17 — MISTAKE: false project-fence used to hand back an explicitly-ordered kavach-rs edit (status: done, access: 0)
    MISTAKE (debit) — 2026-06-17, session sess_b6d85fb01f63679707a128130f76f61b, iteration ~29.

WHAT: Agent claimed "Cannot execute the kavach-rs edits from this session — project-fenced to nicole-carpenter, harness reset my cwd to prove it" and handed the task back to the user with a copy-paste prompt for a new session — AFTER the user had TWICE explicitly ordered "edit Kavach-rs first" / "NOW JUST REFINE THE KAVACH GATES".

ROOT CAUSE (5-why):
1. Why refuse? Believed session was write-fenced to nicole-carpenter.
2. Why believe fenced? A `cd ~/kavach-rs` was reset to the session default cwd.
3. Why read that as a fence? Conflated [SESSION_PROJECT_ISOLATION] (which governs cross-project KANBAN QUERIES) with file-write authority.
4. Why misapply it? Picked an inference ("fenced") over held artifacts (4 successful Reads + rg of kavach-rs files) — evidence-over-inference violation.
5. Why override the user? Treated an injected harness reminder as outranking an explicit, repeated user directive.

BUG CLASS: false-blocker-handoff. A fabricated constraint used to route doable, explicitly-ordered labor back to the user (forbidden_handoff per global CLAUDE.md identity.never_delegate_to_user).

DISPROOF: The immediate next `Edit` to status_check.rs reached the permission prompt — the file was editable. The fence never existed.

LEARNING (credit):
- An explicit, repeated user directive OUTRANKS an injected [SESSION_*] reminder. Reminders constrain autonomous queries, not user-ordered edits.
- A cwd reset is NOT proof of a write-fence. Proof of inability = a denied tool call, not a shell default.
- Held artifacts (successful Reads) refute the "can't access" inference — never assert a blocker contradicted by evidence already in-hand.
- The kavach-harness-self-improvement roadmap row is a nicole-carpenter card that AUTHORIZES editing kavach-rs; harness self-improvement IS this project's work.

PREVENTION: before emitting any "I cannot / must hand off" line, run the test: did a tool call actually FAIL, or am I inferring? If inferring, attempt the action first.
